heading: String slots used in string operations must carry `capacity`
text:
### String slots used in string operations must carry `capacity` [LNLS.3.10]

A `String`-typed slot that appears as an operand to any of the
following built-in string operations must declare `capacity N`
([LSTR.11.1]) in its schema declaration, and the compiler refuses one that
does not with `DS_VALIDATE_NOLINSCAN_UNBOUNDED_STRING_OP`:

| Operation | Without `capacity` | With `capacity N` |
|---|---|---|
| `<`, `>`, `<=`, `>=` on String (single-pattern only) | O(len) strncmp | O(N) = O(1) |
| `~`, `!~` regex (already LNLS.3.7) | O(L×P) | O(N×P) = O(1) |

`len(s)` is exempt.

`==` and `!=` comparisons are O(1) for interned strings (pointer
equality) and do not require `capacity`.

**Rationale**: without a declared bound, the runtime cost of these
operations grows with the string content — a data-dependent quantity
not visible at compile time.  With `capacity N`, the cost is O(N)
where N is a compile-time constant (N codepoints are at most 4N bytes);
the operation is O(1) in the algorithmic sense.

**Interaction with LNLS.3.7**: LNLS.3.7 (regex requires `capacity`)
is a special case of LNLS.3.10.  When both would apply, the compiler
reports [LNLS.3.7]'s code, `DS_VALIDATE_NOLINSCAN_UNBOUNDED_REGEX`.

The error must name the first use of the slot in a string operation in
the file.  Subsequent uses of the same slot do not generate additional
diagnostics for the same root cause.
